```text
▶ outline ready · 20261030-post-invoices-request-lifecycle-map
  A POST /invoices request is read and JSON parsed in `readBody` (`src/http/server.ts:4`)…

  report    work/20261030-post-invoices-request-lifecycle-map/research.md
  findings  13

[a] accept   [p] accept and publish to artifacts/reports/post-invoices-request-lifecycle-map.md   [d] deeper pass   [x] reject: <why>
```

Here is the path: `readBody` in `src/http/server.ts` parses the JSON body, and `Router.handle` in `src/http/router.ts` matches the path segment by segment. The handler in `src/http/handlers.ts` then gets the id from `nextId` (highest id in the file plus one) and writes it with `save`, which rewrites the whole file with `writeFileSync`. The response is 201 with the invoice and its computed `totals`.

On concurrency: two requests in one server process get different ids, because `nextId` and `save` are synchronous with no `await` between them. Two writers on the same file, such as two server instances, can get the same id. One invoice then silently overwrites the other, or one write drops the other's new invoice (R-009). The write is also not atomic (written in place, not via a temp file), so a crash mid-write can leave a truncated file that makes every read fail.

You accepted the outline, so the deep pass did not run. Some points are still open: whether `src/cli.ts` writes to the same file, how totals are computed, and what the existing tests already check. The two concurrency points above are inferred from the code and were not tested by running two requests.
